what_it_does: This paper addresses a resource-waste problem in chips designed specifically to run deep neural networks (AI models built from layers of arithmetic). These chips (called DNN accelerators) typically contain many identical processing cores and fast on-chip memory buffers — small, very fast storage banks sitting right next to the math units. A common scheduling strategy called layer-pipeline mapping runs different layers of the neural network on different cores at the same time, like an assembly line. The problem is that each stage of the pipeline finishes at a different speed, so some cores sit idle while waiting, and their assigned buffer space goes unused. BufferProspector is a tool that first calculates exactly how much buffer space each core actually needs at each pipeline stage, then reassigns the leftover buffer from idle cores to busier ones. By filling those untapped buffers with extra data (like more input tiles), the accelerator can keep more cores productive, improving throughput without adding hardware. The exact speedup numbers are not available from the abstract alone.
